If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating downside risk.

If sentiment flips from negative to positive within 3 days, accelerate upward correction by 1–2% in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect sentiment momentum shift.

If sentiment remains neutral (0.00–0.33) over last 5 days, apply flat correction of ±0.2% for late horizon (16–30 days) to avoid overfitting to recent noise.

If sentiment spikes to 1.00 in last 2 days, add 1–2% upward bias in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect strong bullish sentiment.

If sentiment drops to -0.67 or lower in last 2 days, apply 1–2% downward bias in mid-horizon (8–15 days) to reflect strong bearish sentiment.
